name: Snowflake CLI
description: Protects modern `snow sql` queries, files, stdin, nested sources, data, \ ingestion, compute, and account privileges

destructive_patterns.name: stdin-unverified
destructive_patterns.description: snow sql receives SQL or a source that the engine cannot completely verify.
destructive_patterns.explanation: Materialize the exact rendered SQL, keep all !source inputs local, and review every statement before execution.

destructive_patterns.name: drop-database
destructive_patterns.description: DROP DATABASE removes the database and every contained schema and object.
destructive_patterns.explanation: Snowflake Time Travel and UNDROP are conditional on object support, retention, privileges, and subsequent operations; they are not a substitute for preventing the drop.

destructive_patterns.name: drop-schema
destructive_patterns.description: DROP SCHEMA removes the schema and can remove all contained objects.
destructive_patterns.explanation: Review the schema contents, prefer RESTRICT where supported, and clone the schema before broad DDL.

destructive_patterns.name: drop-table
destructive_patterns.description: DROP TABLE removes the active table and its data.
destructive_patterns.explanation: Verify the fully qualified target, inspect retention, and create a zero-copy clone before dropping the table.

destructive_patterns.name: replace-database
destructive_patterns.description: CREATE OR REPLACE DATABASE replaces a live database.
destructive_patterns.explanation: Create and validate a separate database or clone instead of replacing the active database in place.

destructive_patterns.name: replace-schema
destructive_patterns.description: CREATE OR REPLACE SCHEMA replaces a live schema.
destructive_patterns.explanation: Clone the schema and test the migration against the clone before changing production.

destructive_patterns.name: replace-table
destructive_patterns.description: CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE replaces the active table.
destructive_patterns.explanation: Build and validate a separate table or clone, then use a reviewed cutover operation.

destructive_patterns.name: truncate-table
destructive_patterns.description: TRUNCATE TABLE removes every row from the target table.
destructive_patterns.explanation: Preview the row count and clone the table before truncating it.

destructive_patterns.name: delete-all
destructive_patterns.description: DELETE without a top-level WHERE clause removes every row.
destructive_patterns.explanation: Add a reviewed WHERE predicate and run the equivalent SELECT and COUNT first.

destructive_patterns.name: update-all
destructive_patterns.description: UPDATE without a top-level WHERE clause modifies every row.
destructive_patterns.explanation: Add a reviewed WHERE predicate and preview the exact target rows first.

destructive_patterns.name: drop-data-product
destructive_patterns.description: DROP removes a live view, materialized view, or dynamic table.
destructive_patterns.explanation: Inspect dependencies and validate a replacement object before removing the live query surface.

destructive_patterns.name: drop-ingestion-object
destructive_patterns.description: DROP removes a live stage, pipe, stream, or task.
destructive_patterns.explanation: Inspect pipeline dependencies and state before removing an ingestion or scheduling object.

destructive_patterns.name: drop-warehouse
destructive_patterns.description: DROP WAREHOUSE removes compute used by applications, tasks, or users.
destructive_patterns.explanation: Inspect warehouse consumers and prefer a reversible suspend only after reviewing active workloads.

destructive_patterns.name: drop-principal
destructive_patterns.description: DROP USER or DROP ROLE can break services and revoke access hierarchies.
destructive_patterns.explanation: Review grants and dependencies, then disable access reversibly before deleting a principal.

destructive_patterns.name: drop-security-object
destructive_patterns.description: DROP removes a live integration, network policy, or share.
destructive_patterns.explanation: Review all consumers, grants, and recovery options before removing the security or sharing object.

destructive_patterns.name: drop-programmable-object
destructive_patterns.description: DROP removes a file format, sequence, function, or procedure used by workloads.
destructive_patterns.explanation: Inspect object dependencies and preserve the current definition before removal.

destructive_patterns.name: remove-stage-files
destructive_patterns.description: REMOVE deletes files from an internal Snowflake stage.
destructive_patterns.explanation: LIST the exact stage path and verify retention or a backup before removing files.

destructive_patterns.name: pause-pipe
destructive_patterns.description: ALTER PIPE pauses ingestion and can silently make downstream data stale.
destructive_patterns.explanation: Inspect pipe status and downstream freshness requirements before pausing ingestion.

destructive_patterns.name: suspend-task
destructive_patterns.description: ALTER TASK SUSPEND stops scheduled execution.
destructive_patterns.explanation: Inspect task dependencies and active runs before suspending the task.

destructive_patterns.name: execute-task
destructive_patterns.description: EXECUTE TASK immediately starts a task run and may cascade a task graph.
destructive_patterns.explanation: Inspect the task definition, owner privileges, graph dependencies, and active runs before forcing execution.

destructive_patterns.name: suspend-warehouse
destructive_patterns.description: ALTER WAREHOUSE SUSPEND can interrupt active or queued workloads.
destructive_patterns.explanation: Inspect active queries and dependent tasks before suspending compute.

destructive_patterns.name: broad-revoke
destructive_patterns.description: REVOKE removes broad privileges or role membership and can break applications immediately.
destructive_patterns.explanation: Review current grants and identify every affected principal before revoking access.

destructive_patterns.name: broad-grant
destructive_patterns.description: GRANT creates account-wide, all-privilege, or ACCOUNTADMIN access.
destructive_patterns.explanation: Grant only the required privileges on specific objects to a least-privilege role.

destructive_patterns.name: transfer-ownership
destructive_patterns.description: GRANT OWNERSHIP transfers control and can revoke or copy existing grants.
destructive_patterns.explanation: Inventory outbound privileges and review COPY/REVOKE CURRENT GRANTS semantics before transferring ownership.

destructive_patterns.name: alter-table-drop-column
destructive_patterns.description: ALTER TABLE DROP COLUMN removes a column and its active data.
destructive_patterns.explanation: Clone the table and validate all downstream consumers before removing the column.

destructive_patterns.name: alter-table-swap
destructive_patterns.description: ALTER TABLE SWAP WITH exchanges table identities atomically.
destructive_patterns.explanation: Verify both fully qualified tables and compare row counts and schemas before swapping.

destructive_patterns.name: insert-overwrite
destructive_patterns.description: INSERT OVERWRITE replaces the target table's current rows.
destructive_patterns.explanation: Write to and validate a separate table before a reviewed cutover.

destructive_patterns.name: copy-overwrite
destructive_patterns.description: COPY INTO a location with OVERWRITE = TRUE can replace exported files.
destructive_patterns.explanation: Export to a versioned path and LIST the destination before copying.

destructive_patterns.name: put-overwrite
destructive_patterns.description: PUT with OVERWRITE = TRUE can replace files in an internal stage.
destructive_patterns.explanation: Upload to a versioned stage path and LIST existing files first.

destructive_patterns.name: replace-live-object
destructive_patterns.description: CREATE OR REPLACE replaces a live Snowflake object and may lose grants, state, or configuration.
destructive_patterns.explanation: Create and validate a separate object before changing the live definition.

destructive_patterns.name: bounded-delete
destructive_patterns.description: DELETE mutates every row selected by its WHERE predicate.
destructive_patterns.explanation: Run the equivalent SELECT and COUNT against a clone before deleting rows.

destructive_patterns.name: bounded-update
destructive_patterns.description: UPDATE mutates every row selected by its WHERE predicate.
destructive_patterns.explanation: Preview affected rows and validate the update against a clone first.

destructive_patterns.name: merge-data
destructive_patterns.description: MERGE can update, insert, or delete rows based on source matching.
destructive_patterns.explanation: Validate source uniqueness and preview matched and unmatched rows against a clone.

destructive_patterns.name: copy-into-table
destructive_patterns.description: COPY INTO a table can load duplicate, corrupt, or unexpected data.
destructive_patterns.explanation: Validate the staged files and load into a clone or scratch table first.

destructive_patterns.name: rename-object
destructive_patterns.description: Renaming a database, schema, or table can break fully qualified consumers.
destructive_patterns.explanation: Inventory consumers and stage a coordinated cutover before renaming the object.

destructive_patterns.name: alter-column
destructive_patterns.description: ALTER TABLE ALTER COLUMN can break writes and downstream consumers.
destructive_patterns.explanation: Validate type, nullability, default, and policy changes against a clone first.

destructive_patterns.name: warehouse-settings
destructive_patterns.description: ALTER WAREHOUSE SET can create availability or cost risk.
destructive_patterns.explanation: Review active consumers, size, scaling, and auto-suspend settings before applying changes.

destructive_patterns.name: abort-query
destructive_patterns.description: !abort cancels an active Snowflake query.
destructive_patterns.explanation: Inspect query history and confirm the exact query ID before aborting it.

destructive_patterns.name: interactive-edit
destructive_patterns.description: !edit executes SQL modified in an external editor that the engine cannot inspect in advance.
destructive_patterns.explanation: Materialize the final SQL in a reviewed local file and execute it with snow sql -f.

destructive_patterns.name: execute-immediate
destructive_patterns.description: EXECUTE IMMEDIATE runs generated SQL whose rendered semantics require explicit review.
destructive_patterns.explanation: Materialize and review the exact rendered SQL, including templates and variables, before executing it.

destructive_patterns.name: cli-object-drop-database
destructive_patterns.description: snow object drop database/schema removes the object and everything inside it.
destructive_patterns.explanation: Dropping a database or schema removes ALL contained objects (tables, views, \ stages, pipes, tasks, functions). Time Travel/UNDROP recovery is conditional \ on retention, edition, and privileges - it is not a substitute for preventing \ the drop. Verify with `snow object list database` / `snow object describe` \ and consider `CREATE DATABASE <name>_backup CLONE <name>` first.

destructive_patterns.name: cli-object-drop
destructive_patterns.description: snow object drop permanently removes a Snowflake object.
destructive_patterns.explanation: snow object drop removes tables, views, stages, streams, tasks, warehouses, \ users, roles, integrations, and more; --force skips the confirmation prompt. \ Dropping shared infrastructure can break applications and automation \ immediately. Inspect first with `snow object describe <type> <name>`.

destructive_patterns.name: cli-stage-drop
destructive_patterns.description: snow stage drop removes the stage; internal staged files are not recoverable.
destructive_patterns.explanation: Dropped stages cannot be recovered - internal stage files are gone, and \ workflows (COPY INTO, Snowpipe) referencing the stage break immediately. \ List contents first with `snow stage list-files <stage>`.

destructive_patterns.name: cli-stage-remove
destructive_patterns.description: snow stage remove deletes files from a stage.
destructive_patterns.explanation: Files removed from an internal stage are not covered by Time Travel. \ Ingestion pipelines expecting those files will silently see nothing to \ load. Preview with `snow stage list-files <stage>` and consider copying \ the files out first.

destructive_patterns.name: cli-app-teardown
destructive_patterns.description: snow app teardown drops the Native App and (with --cascade) its owned objects.
destructive_patterns.explanation: snow app teardown drops the application object and the application \ package's development artifacts; with --cascade it also drops objects the \ app owns, databases included. Anyone using the app loses access \ immediately.

destructive_patterns.name: cli-app-version-drop
destructive_patterns.description: snow app version drop removes a Native App version definition.
destructive_patterns.explanation: Dropping an application package version prevents new installs and upgrades \ of that version; releases pinned to it break.

destructive_patterns.name: cli-snowpark-drop
destructive_patterns.description: snow snowpark drop removes a deployed procedure or function from Snowflake.
destructive_patterns.explanation: snow snowpark drop function/procedure drops the named object from \ Snowflake. Downstream callers (tasks, other procedures, applications) \ fail until it is redeployed.

destructive_patterns.name: cli-spcs-drop
destructive_patterns.description: snow spcs ... drop removes container services infrastructure.
destructive_patterns.explanation: Dropping an SPCS service stops and removes the running workload; dropping \ a compute pool removes the compute for every service on it; dropping an \ image repository deletes the stored images.

destructive_patterns.name: cli-dbt-drop
destructive_patterns.description: snow dbt drop removes a dbt project object from Snowflake.
destructive_patterns.explanation: snow dbt drop removes the named DBT PROJECT object; scheduled `snow dbt \ execute` runs and tasks referencing it fail until it is redeployed.

destructive_patterns.name: cli-dcm-drop
destructive_patterns.description: snow dcm drop removes a DCM project object from Snowflake.
destructive_patterns.explanation: snow dcm drop removes the named DCM PROJECT object, including its \ deployment history in Snowflake.
